title: Sovereignty Policy Enforcer + Evidence Stream for Config Drift Detection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a reconciler + evidence pipeline to ensure data sovereignty and retention policies are enforced across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The system should detect configuration drift of residency and retention settings, auto-remediate where allowed, and generate cryptographically-signed evidence artifacts for audits. The feature is intended to operate as a Policy-as-Code control with a GitOps workflow for policy changes and a streaming evidence store for compliance reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Policy definitions live in a dedicated repo as Rego or YAML policy artifacts and trigger CI validation on PRs
A controller continuously evaluates account-level and deployment-level configs (region tags, retention TTLs, KMS key residency) and surfaces violations in Console and the compliance dashboard
Drift remediation supports two modes: 'auto-fix' (applies change) and 'alert-only' (creates ticket and evidence) configurable per-policy and per-customer tier

Every remediation or alert creation emits an evidence artifact containing: policy_id, detected_value, desired_value, timestamp, actor (controller/engineer), and a signature stored in WORM storage for 7 years
Console shows last-evaluated timestamp per-account, list of active violations, and link to evidence artifacts; RBAC prevents non-compliance-admins from deleting evidence
Endpoint and metrics expose counts of drift events, remediation success rate, and mean time to remediate (MTTR)
decisions: Use OPA (Rego) for policy evaluation to leverage existing team expertise and expressiveness for residency/retention rules
Policies will be authorable via YAML-backed Rego templates in a single 'silver' policy repo with GitOps flows; policy changes require CODEOWNERS review for security team
Evidence artifacts will be signed with our HSM-backed signing key and stored in an immutable S3 bucket with lifecycle rules for retention
Controller will be deployed in a multi-tenant mode: per-region workers to reduce cross-region egress and respect residency boundaries
Initial remediation actions limited to non-destructive config updates (e.g., set retention TTLs, flip region flags). Destructive or data-moving actions require manual approval workflow
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (MVP): policy repo, evaluation service, Console violations UI, evidence writer + storage, metrics. No automatic data transfer/removal in MVP
Phase 2: auto-fix agents for Dedicated control plane and Private installer hooks for on-prem customers, plus audit exports and scheduled reporting
Will extend runtime config model to include 'residency_tag' and 'retention_policy_id' fields and add schema validation to API layer
Controller will call existing config-management APIs rather than directly mutating infra; use existing service accounts and audit log paths
Backwards compatibility: if a deployment lacks the new residency metadata, controller will mark 'unknown' and create a low-severity violation to be triaged
qa_plan: Unit tests for Rego policies and policy loader, 95%+ coverage for evaluation paths
Integration tests exercising detection, alert-only flow, and evidence generation against a mocked config API
E2E tests in staging with a private cluster that simulates region mislabeling and incorrect TTLs
Table-driven tests to validate signature verification and immutability of evidence artifacts
rollout_plan: Start with internal orgs (redwood-internal) in 'alert-only' mode for 2 weeks
Enable 'auto-fix' on low-risk policies for beta customers with opt-in flag
Gradually expand to all Hosted customers while monitoring MTTR and false positive rate
Communicate breaking policy changes via release notes and policy PR changelog; provide a 2-week freeze window before enforcement
monitoring: Alert: >1% false-positive rate over 24h for any policy -> paging to SRE/Compliance
Dashboard: median time between detection and remediation, signed evidence creation latency
